subject: Create multiple (separate) plots in one session

messages.author: 0b8deed76b95a362
messages.subject: Create multiple (separate) plots in one session
parts:
I have a situation in which I have to produce 15 or 20 graphs for each
of several datasets. The commands are the same each time; only the data
differs. What I've been doing is to copy the commands for each plot
into R, copying the result as a bmp, pasting that into a MS word file,
removing that plot and creating the next one. This gets tedious.

Is there a way by which I could paste the commands for all the plots
into R, and have them all be available on my screen? That doesn't seem
to be happening now. If I copy commands to create multiple plots, only
the last one shows up.
Thanks for any help.
David

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: Create multiple (separate) plots in one session
parts:
A couple easy options I can think of:
  • Plot them all using an RStudio R session. The "Plots" tab keeps all plots in a session and you can use the arrows to cycle through each of them.
  • Use `ggsave` to write them to disk, then use your OS to cycle through them. For example, on a Mac, use Quickview.

Cheers,
Doug

messages.author: 2710b717e5dbb066
messages.subject: Re: Create multiple (separate) plots in one session
parts:
Here are a couple more suggestions (in addition to Doug's).

You can send a plot directly to a file using functions like pdf,
bitmap, png, jpeg, tif, bmp, etc. With the bmp and other bitmap based
functions you can specify a filename that will increment with each
plot. For example if you do bmp(filename='myplots%03d.bmp') then the
first plot will go into a file named myplots001.bmp, the second plot
will go into the file myplots002.bmp, and so forth. Just remember to
do a dev.off() after the last plot to finalize the last file. This
way you can loop through a bunch of plots and datasets and each plot
will be in its own file.

If you use the pdf graphics device then you can produce a single pdf
document with one plot per page. It may be sufficient to send this to
the client, or you could copy and paste from the pdf or use other
tools to extract the plots or convert to a word document.

Another option is to use the knitr package along with the pandoc
program (or possibly the new Rmarkdown package). This way you can
create a document with all the plots and convert it directly to a word
document.

The pander package is another option for looping through and sending
plots to a word document.

There is also an R2wd package for writing to word documents, however
one of the possible packages it uses is not free, so be careful of the
usage.
